title.en: Volume 177 Biographies 64: Zhang Siming, Wu Yuangui, Zhang Sheng, Zang Mengjie, Chen Hao
title.raw: 卷一百七十七 列傳第六十四: 張思明 吳元珪 張昇 臧夢解 陳顥 Volume 177 Biographies 64: Zhang Siming, Wu Yuangui, Zhang Sheng, Zang Mengjie, Chen Hao

sentences.zh: 張思明

translations.literal: Zhang Siming
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Siming

sentences.zh: 張思明，字士瞻，其先獲嘉人，後​​徙居輝州。

translations.literal: Zhang Siming, courtesy name Shizhan, his ancestors were from Huojia, and later moved to reside in Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Siming, whose courtesy name was Shizhan, came from a family originally of Huojia that later relocated to Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 思明穎悟過人，讀書日記千言。

translations.literal: Siming was exceptionally quick-witted beyond others; in reading books he could memorize a thousand words per day.
translations.idiomatic: Siming was unusually gifted; when he read, he could commit a thousand characters to memory in a single day.

sentences.zh: 至元十九年，由侍儀司舍人辟御史臺掾，又辟尚書省掾。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Zhiyuan, from his post as usher of the Ceremonial Institute he was recruited as clerk of the Censorate, and again recruited as clerk of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 1282, while serving as an usher in the Ceremonial Institute, he was recruited first as a clerk in the Censorate and then in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 左丞相阿合馬既死，世祖追咎其奸欺，命尚書簿問遺孽。

translations.literal: After Left Chancellor Ahmad died, Shizu pursued blame for his treachery and fraud, ordering the Secretariat to register and interrogate his surviving accomplices.
translations.idiomatic: After the Left Chancellor Ahmad was dead, Kublai held him accountable for his deceit and ordered the Secretariat to investigate and record his remaining associates.

sentences.zh: 一日，召右丞何榮祖、左丞馬紹，盡輸其贓以入，思明抱牘從，日已昏，命讀之，自昏達曙，帝聽忘疲，曰：「讀人吐音，大似侍儀舍人。

translations.literal: One day he summoned Right Chancellor He Rongzu and Left Chancellor Ma Shao to submit all their bribes in full; Siming carried documents and followed. The day had already grown dark; he ordered them read aloud—from dusk until dawn. The Emperor listened, forgetting fatigue, and said: "The reader's enunciation greatly resembles a Ceremonial Institute usher."
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion the Emperor summoned the Right Chancellor He Rongzu and the Left Chancellor Ma Shao to turn in all their illicit gains. Siming followed with the documents in his arms. Night had fallen, yet the Emperor ordered them read aloud, and listened from dusk until dawn without tiring. He remarked, "The reader's delivery sounds very much like one of our Ceremonial Institute ushers."

sentences.zh: 」右丞對曰：「正由舍人選為掾。

translations.literal: " The Right Chancellor replied: "It is precisely because he was selected from among the ushers to become a clerk."
translations.idiomatic: " The Right Chancellor answered, "That is because he was chosen from among the ushers for this clerkship."

sentences.zh: 」帝奇之，曰：「斯人可用。

translations.literal: " The Emperor marveled at him and said: "This man can be used."
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor was impressed and said, "This man is fit for service."

sentences.zh: 」明日，擢為大都路治中。

translations.literal: " The next day he was promoted to Assistant Administrator of the Dadu Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: " The following day Siming was promoted to Assistant Administrator of the Dadu metropolitan circuit.

sentences.zh: 思明以超遷逾等，固辭，乃改湖廣行省都事。

translations.literal: Siming, because the promotion exceeded his proper rank, firmly declined, and was therefore transferred to be Chief Secretary of the Huguang Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Siming declined firmly on the grounds that the promotion skipped too many ranks, and was instead appointed Chief Secretary of the Huguang Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 元貞元年，召為中書省檢校，六曹無滯案，遷戶部主事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanzhen he was summoned as Reviewer of the Central Secretariat; in the six bureaus there were no backlog cases, and he was transferred to be Principal Clerk of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In 1295 he was recalled to serve as a reviewer in the Central Secretariat, where he cleared every bureau's backlog of cases and was promoted to principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 大德初，擢左司都事，有獻西域秤法，思明以惑眾不用。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dade he was promoted to Chief Secretary of the Left Secretariat; someone presented a Western Regions method of weighing, and Siming, holding that it would mislead the people, did not adopt it.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dade reign he rose to chief secretary of the Left Secretariat. When someone proposed a new weighing system from the Western Regions, Siming refused to adopt it, judging that it would only confuse the public.

sentences.zh: 初立海道運糧萬戶府於江浙，受除者憚涉險，不行，思明請升等以優之，因著為令。

translations.literal: When the Maritime Grain Transport Ten-thousand Households Office was first established in Jiang-Zhe, those who received appointments feared the perils of the voyage and would not go; Siming requested raising their rank grades as an incentive, and this was accordingly written into regulation.
translations.idiomatic: When the maritime grain-transport office was first set up in Jiang-Zhe, appointees shrank from the dangers of the sea route and refused to take up their posts. Siming urged that their rank be raised as an incentive, and the measure was enacted as law.

sentences.zh: 五年，轉吏部郎中。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to be Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the reign he was transferred to director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 九年，改集賢司直。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was changed to Direct Attendant of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was reassigned as direct attendant of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.

sentences.zh: 十年，除江浙行中書省左右司郎中。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed Director of the Left and Right Secretariats of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was appointed director in the left and right secretariats of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十一年春，兩浙大饑，首贊發廩賑之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eleventh year, the two Zhe regions suffered great famine; he was the first to urge opening the granaries to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eleventh year both Zhe regions were stricken by severe famine, and he was the first to urge opening the public granaries for relief.

sentences.zh: 至大三年，遷兩浙鹽運使，未上，入參議樞密院事，改中書省左司郎中。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhida he was transferred to Salt Transport Commissioner of the two Zhe regions; before taking up the post he entered to serve as Discussant of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and was changed to Director of the Left Secretariat of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 1310 he was appointed salt transport commissioner for the two Zhe regions, but before he could take up that post he was made a discussant in the Bureau of Military Affairs and then director of the Central Secretariat's left office.

sentences.zh: 皇慶元年，再授兩浙鹽運使，歲課羨贏，僚屬請上增數，思明曰：「贏縮不常，萬一以增為額，是我希一己之榮，遺百世之害。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangqing he was again appointed Salt Transport Commissioner of the two Zhe regions. That year's tax receipts exceeded the quota, and his subordinates asked to report the increase; Siming said: "Surplus and shortfall are not constant; if by chance the increase were made the fixed quota, this would be my seeking personal glory at the cost of harm lasting a hundred generations."
translations.idiomatic: In 1312 he was again appointed salt commissioner for the two Zhe regions. When that year's receipts ran above quota, his staff urged reporting the surplus as a permanent increase. Siming objected: "Revenues rise and fall; if we lock in a bumper year as the standard quota, I would be trading a moment's credit for generations of harm."

sentences.zh: 」二年，召為戶部尚書。

translations.literal: " In the second year he was summoned to be Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: " The following year he was recalled to serve as Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 延祐元年，進參議中書省事；

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanyou he was advanced to Discussant of Central Secretariat Affairs;
translations.idiomatic: In 1314 he was promoted to discussant of Central Secretariat affairs;

sentences.zh: 三年，拜中書參知政事。

translations.literal: in the third year he was appointed Assistant Administrator of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: and in the third year he was appointed assistant administrator of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，浮屠妙總統有寵，敕中書官其弟五品，思明執不可。

translations.literal: When Renzong took the throne, the Buddhist monk Miao Zongtong enjoyed favor; an edict ordered the Secretariat to grant his younger brother a fifth-rank office, and Siming firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: After Renzong came to the throne, the Buddhist monk Miao Zongtong was in high favor, and an edict directed the Secretariat to give his younger brother a fifth-rank post. Siming stood firm and would not comply.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，召見切責之，對曰：「選法，天下公器。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly angered, summoned him, and sharply rebuked him. He replied: "The selection law is a public instrument of the realm."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was furious, summoned him, and rebuked him sharply. Siming answered, "The law of appointment is a public trust belonging to the whole realm."

sentences.zh: 徑路一開，來者雜遝。

translations.literal: Once a shortcut is opened, those who come will crowd in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Once one back door is opened, petitioners will pour in without end.

sentences.zh: 故寧違旨獲戾，不忍隳祖宗成憲，使四方得窺陛下淺深也。

translations.literal: Therefore I would rather disobey the edict and incur blame than bear to destroy the established statutes of the ancestors and let the four quarters glimpse the depth or shallowness of Your Majesty's resolve.
translations.idiomatic: I would rather defy your order and accept punishment than tear down the statutes our forefathers left us and let the empire gauge how deep or shallow your Majesty's principles run.

sentences.zh: 」帝心然其言，而業已許之，曰：「卿可姑與之，後勿為例。

translations.literal: " The Emperor inwardly approved his words, but having already promised, said: "You may for the moment grant it to him; afterward do not make this a precedent."
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor was persuaded in his heart, yet having already given his word he said, "Grant it for now, but do not let this become a precedent."

sentences.zh: 」乃為萬億庫提舉，不與散官。

translations.literal: " He was therefore made Superintendent of the Myriad Myriads Treasury, without being given a regular civil rank.
translations.idiomatic: " The brother was given the post of superintendent of the Myriad Myriads Treasury, but no regular civil rank.

sentences.zh: 久之，近臣疾其持法峭直，日構讒間，出為工部尚書。

translations.literal: After a long while, court favorites resented his stern and upright enforcement of law and daily wove slander between them, and he was sent out to be Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, favorites at court, resenting his rigid adherence to law, slandered him day after day until he was transferred out to serve as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 帝問左右曰：「張士瞻居工部，得無怏怏乎？

translations.literal: The Emperor asked those around him: "Now that Zhang Shizhan is in the Ministry of Works, is he perhaps discontent?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked his attendants, "With Zhang Shizhan in the Ministry of Works, is he perhaps sulking?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「勤政如初。

translations.literal: " They replied: "He is diligent in government as at first."
translations.idiomatic: " They answered, "He is as diligent in office as ever."

sentences.zh: 」帝嘉嘆之，命授宣政院副使。

translations.literal: " The Emperor praised and sighed over this, and ordered him appointed Vice Commissioner of the Commission for Buddhist and Tibetan Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor expressed his admiration and ordered him appointed vice commissioner of the Commission for Buddhist and Tibetan Affairs.

sentences.zh: 五年，除西京宣慰使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed Pacification Commissioner of the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was appointed pacification commissioner of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 嶺北戍士多貧者，歲凶，相挺為變，思明威惠並行，邊境乃安。

translations.literal: Many of the garrison soldiers north of the ranges were poor; in a year of famine they stirred one another to mutiny. Siming combined stern authority with gracious kindness, and the borderlands were thereby pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Many frontier garrison troops north of the ranges were destitute; when famine struck they rose together in unrest. Siming combined firm discipline with generous relief, and the border was restored to peace.

sentences.zh: 因疏和林運糧不便事十一條，帝勞以端硯、上尊。

translations.literal: He thereupon memorialized eleven points on the inconveniences of grain transport to Karakorum, and the Emperor rewarded him with an inkstone of duan stone and fine wine.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a memorial listing eleven problems with grain transport to Karakorum, and the Emperor rewarded him with a duan inkstone and fine wine.

sentences.zh: 會左丞相哈散辭職，帝不允，其請益堅，帝詰之曰：「朕任卿未專邪？

translations.literal: It happened that Left Chancellor Hasan resigned his post; the Emperor would not permit it, but his request grew ever firmer. The Emperor questioned him, saying: "Have I not entrusted you with full authority?"
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Left Chancellor Hasan sought to resign; the Emperor refused, but Hasan pressed his request all the more insistently. The Emperor demanded, "Have I not given you my full trust?"

translations.literal: " He said: "No."
translations.idiomatic: " Hasan replied, "No."

sentences.zh: 」曰：「近臣有撓政者邪？

translations.literal: " He said: "Are there favorites near the throne who interfere with government?"
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor asked, "Are there court favorites obstructing your work?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「無有也。

translations.literal: " He said: "There are none."
translations.idiomatic: " Hasan answered, "There are not."

sentences.zh: 」「然則何為而辭？

translations.literal: " "Then why resign?"
translations.idiomatic: " "Then why do you insist on resigning?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣自揆才薄，恐誤陛下國事，若必欲任臣，願荐一人為助。

translations.literal: " He replied: "I myself judge my talent slight and fear I may err in Your Majesty's state affairs; if you must employ me, I wish to recommend one man to assist."
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "I find my own abilities wanting and fear I may harm your Majesty's governance. If you must keep me in office, I beg leave to recommend one man to assist me."

sentences.zh: 」帝問：「為誰？

translations.literal: " The Emperor asked: "Who is it?"
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor asked, "Whom do you have in mind?"

sentences.zh: 朕能從汝。

translations.literal: I can follow your recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: I will do as you say.

sentences.zh: 」哈散再拜謝曰；

translations.literal: " Hasan bowed twice in thanks and said:
translations.idiomatic: " Hasan bowed twice and said,

sentences.zh: 「臣願得張思明。

translations.literal: "I wish to have Zhang Siming."
translations.idiomatic: "I ask for Zhang Siming."

sentences.zh: 」即日拜思明中書參知政事。

translations.literal: " That same day Siming was appointed Assistant Administrator of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: " That same day Siming was appointed assistant administrator of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 比召至，車駕幸上都，見於道，慰勉之曰：「卿向不負朕注委，故朕用哈散言，復起汝。

translations.literal: By the time he was summoned and arrived, the imperial carriage was proceeding to Shangdu; he was received on the road. The Emperor comforted and encouraged him, saying: "You have not failed the trust I placed in you; therefore I followed Hasan's words and raised you again."
translations.idiomatic: When he was summoned and came up, the Emperor was already on the road to Shangdu and received him along the way. He encouraged him, saying, "You never betrayed the trust I placed in you, and that is why I took Hasan's advice and brought you back."

sentences.zh: 」未幾，升左丞。

translations.literal: " Before long he was promoted to Left Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long he was promoted to Left Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，英宗宅憂，右丞相帖木迭兒用事，日誅大臣不附己者，中外洶洶。

translations.literal: The Emperor died; Yingzong was in mourning seclusion. Right Chancellor Temür Odjir held power and daily executed great ministers who did not attach themselves to him; within and without the court there was great alarm.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor died, Yingzong was still in mourning. The Right Chancellor Temür Odjir seized power and day after day executed ministers who would not follow him, until the whole court was in uproar.

sentences.zh: 思明諫曰：「山陵甫畢，新君未立，丞相恣行殺戮，國人皆謂陰有不臣之心。

translations.literal: Siming remonstrated, saying: "The imperial tomb has only just been completed and the new ruler is not yet established; the Chancellor indulges in executions at will, and the people of the realm all say he secretly harbors disloyal intent."
translations.idiomatic: Siming admonished him: "The imperial tomb rites have only just ended and the new sovereign is not yet enthroned. For the Chancellor to kill at will makes everyone in the realm suspect disloyal ambitions."

sentences.zh: 萬一諸王駙馬疑而不至，將奈之何？

translations.literal: If by chance the princes and imperial sons-in-law grow suspicious and do not come, what then can be done?
translations.idiomatic: If the princes and imperial sons-in-law grow suspicious and refuse to attend, what will you do then?

sentences.zh: 不可不熟慮也。

translations.literal: This cannot but be carefully considered.
translations.idiomatic: You must think this through carefully.

sentences.zh: 」眾皆危之，帖木迭兒大悟曰：「非左丞言，幾誤吾事。

translations.literal: " All thought him in peril, but Temür Odjir came to a great awakening and said: "Had it not been for the Left Chancellor's words, I would nearly have ruined my undertaking."
translations.idiomatic: " Everyone feared for Siming's safety, but Temür Odjir was deeply shaken and said, "Without the Left Chancellor's warning I would nearly have ruined everything."

sentences.zh: 」帝造壽安山寺，監察御史觀音保、瑣咬兒哈的迷失、成珪、李謙亨強諫，帝震怒，殺觀音保、瑣咬兒哈的迷失，以成珪、李謙亨屬吏，思明白丞相曰：「言事，御史職也，祖宗已來，未嘗殺諫臣。

translations.literal: " The Emperor built Shou'an Temple. Investigating Censors Guanyinbao, Suo'er Ha'dimishi, Cheng Gui, and Li Qianheng remonstrated forcefully. The Emperor was greatly angered and executed Guanyinbao and Suo'er Ha'dimishi, handing Cheng Gui and Li Qianheng over to the judicial officials. Siming told the Chancellor plainly: "Speaking on affairs of state is the censor's duty; since the ancestors' time, remonstrating ministers have never been killed."
translations.idiomatic: " When the Emperor undertook construction of Shou'an Temple, the investigating censors Guanyinbao, Suo'er Ha'dimishi, Cheng Gui, and Li Qianheng remonstrated forcefully. The Emperor was enraged and put Guanyinbao and Suo'er Ha'dimishi to death, handing Cheng Gui and Li Qianheng over to the courts. Siming told the Chancellor plainly, "It is a censor's duty to speak out on public affairs. Since the founding of the dynasty, no remonstrating minister has ever been executed."

sentences.zh: 」成、李既屬吏，當論法，丞相乃力言之，二人得從輕典。

translations.literal: " Cheng and Li, having been handed to the officials, should have been judged by law; the Chancellor thereupon spoke forcefully on their behalf, and the two men were able to receive lenient punishment.
translations.idiomatic: " Once Cheng and Li were in the hands of the judicial officials, Siming pressed the Chancellor hard on their behalf, and the two received lighter sentences.

sentences.zh: 及拜住為左丞相，與帖木迭兒各樹朋黨，賊害忠良，思明懼禍及，累表辭，不獲，後竟誣以不支蒙古子女口糧，餓死四百人，遂廢於家，杜門六年。

translations.literal: When Bayiju became Left Chancellor, he and Temür Odjir each formed factions and harmed loyal and worthy men. Siming feared disaster would reach him and repeatedly submitted memorials to resign without success. Later he was falsely accused of failing to supply grain rations for Mongol children, four hundred of whom starved to death; he was therefore dismissed to his home and shut his door for six years.
translations.idiomatic: When Bayiju became Left Chancellor, he and Temür Odjir each built factions and destroyed loyal ministers. Fearing he would be caught up in the purge, Siming repeatedly asked to resign but was refused. He was eventually framed on the charge that four hundred Mongol children had starved because he failed to supply their rations. Dismissed to his home, he lived behind closed doors for six years.

sentences.zh: 思明平生不治產，不畜財，收書三萬七千餘卷；

translations.literal: Throughout his life Siming did not manage estates or hoard wealth; he collected more than thirty-seven thousand volumes of books;
translations.idiomatic: Siming never managed property or hoarded wealth in his lifetime; he amassed a library of more than thirty-seven thousand volumes;

sentences.zh: 尤明於律，與謝仲和、曹鼎新同稱三絕。

translations.literal: he was especially expert in law, and together with Xie Zhonghe and Cao Dingxin was called one of the Three Unrivaled.
translations.idiomatic: and was especially renowned for his mastery of law; together with Xie Zhonghe and Cao Dingxin he was known as one of the Three Unrivaled.

sentences.zh: 贈推忠翊治守義功臣，依前中書左丞、上護軍、清河郡公，諡貞敏。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted the title Meritorious Subject Who Promotes Loyalty, Assists Governance, and Upholds Righteousness, retaining his former ranks as Left Chancellor of the Central Secretariat, Senior Guardian General, and Duke of Qinghe, with the posthumous name Zhenmin.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously honored as a meritorious subject who promoted loyalty, assisted governance, and upheld righteousness, with his former titles of Left Chancellor, Senior Guardian General, and Duke of Qinghe restored, and was given the posthumous name Zhenmin, "Upright and Keen."

sentences.zh: ○吳元珪

translations.literal: ○ Wu Yuangui
translations.idiomatic: ○ Wu Yuangui

sentences.zh: 吳元珪，字君璋，廣平人。

translations.literal: Wu Yuangui, courtesy name Junzhang, was a man of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yuangui, whose courtesy name was Junzhang, was a native of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 父鼎，燕南提刑按察副使。

translations.literal: His father Ding was Vice Commissioner of the Yannan Circuit for Punishments and Investigations.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ding had served as vice commissioner of the Yannan circuit for punishments and investigations.

sentences.zh: 元珪簡重，好深沉之思，凡徵謀治法、律令章程，皆得於家庭之所授受。

translations.literal: Yuangui was reserved and grave, fond of deep reflection; all matters of policy, law, statutes, and regulations he received from instruction within the family.
translations.idiomatic: Yuangui was reserved and serious, inclined to deep reflection; he learned statecraft, law, and administrative procedure entirely through instruction in his own household.

sentences.zh: 至元十四年，世祖召見，命侍左右，授後衛經歷，佩金符。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhiyuan, Shizu summoned him for audience, ordered him to attend at his side, appointed him Administrator of the Rear Guard, and bestowed a gold tally.
translations.idiomatic: In 1277 Kublai summoned him to court, kept him in attendance at his side, appointed him administrator of the Rear Guard, and granted him a gold tally.

sentences.zh: 十七年，從幸上都，受命取禦藥於大都萬歲山，元珪乘傳，未盡一晝夜而至。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he accompanied the imperial progress to Shangdu and was ordered to fetch imperial medicine from Wansui Mountain in Dadu; Yuangui traveled by relay post and arrived in less than a day and night.
translations.idiomatic: In 1280, while accompanying the court to Shangdu, he was sent to fetch imperial medicine from Wansui Mountain in Dadu. Traveling by relay post, he arrived in less than a full day and night.

sentences.zh: 帝奇其速，擢樞密都事，升經歷。

translations.literal: The Emperor marveled at his speed, promoted him to Chief Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and advanced him to Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was astonished at his speed, promoted him to chief secretary in the Bureau of Military Affairs, and then to administrator.

sentences.zh: 嘗從同知樞密院事俺伯進西蕃鎧甲，帝問其制度，元珪應對詳明，帝益奇之。

translations.literal: Once he followed Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Anbo in presenting Western Regions armor; the Emperor asked about its design, and Yuangui answered in full detail, so that the Emperor marveled at him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion he accompanied Vice Director Anbo in presenting Tibetan armor at court. When the Emperor asked about its design, Yuangui answered in meticulous detail and impressed him still more.

sentences.zh: 初，江南既定，樞密奏裁定官屬，京師五衛、行省、萬戶府設官有差，均俸祿，給醫藥，設學校，置屯田，多元珪所論建。

translations.literal: When the south of the Yangtze was first pacified, the Bureau of Military Affairs memorialized to fix the official establishment; for the Five Guards of the capital, branch secretariats, and ten-thousand-household offices, offices were established with distinctions, salaries were equalized, medicine was supplied, schools were set up, and garrison fields were established—most of these were proposals Yuangui discussed and established.
translations.idiomatic: After the south was pacified, the Bureau of Military Affairs submitted plans to fix the official establishment for the Five Guards, branch secretariats, and ten-thousand-household offices—standardizing salaries, supplying medicine, founding schools, and establishing garrison farms. Most of these measures originated in Yuangui's proposals.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，參議樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he became Discussant of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he was made a discussant in the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時繕修宮城，尚書省奏役軍士萬人，留守司主之。

translations.literal: At that time the palace city was being repaired; the Secretariat memorialized to employ ten thousand soldiers, with the Capital Guard Commission supervising.
translations.idiomatic: While the palace city was under repair, the Secretariat proposed drafting ten thousand soldiers under the Capital Guard Commission.

sentences.zh: 元珪亟陳其不便，乃立武衛，繕理宮城，以留守段天祐兼都指揮使，凡有興作，必以聞於樞府。

translations.literal: Yuangui urgently stated the inconveniences of this, whereupon the Martial Guard was established to repair the palace city; Capital Guardian Duan Tianyou was concurrently made Commander-in-Chief, and for every construction project report had to be made to the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yuangui protested vigorously that this was unworkable. A Martial Guard was therefore established to handle palace repairs, with Capital Guardian Duan Tianyou as its commander-in-chief, and every construction project had to be reported to the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋升樞密院判官。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 奏定萬戶用軍士八人，千戶四人，百戶二人，多役者有罰。

translations.literal: He memorialized to fix that a ten-thousand-household commander might use eight soldiers, a thousand-household commander four, and a hundred-household commander two; those who over-employed labor were punished.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized fixing the quota of soldiers each commander might employ—eight for a ten-thousand-household commander, four for a thousand-household commander, two for a hundred-household commander—with penalties for excess labor.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，除禮部侍郎，遷左司郎中。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites and transferred to Director of the Left Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he was appointed vice minister of rites and then transferred to director of the Left Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，參議中書省事。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he became Discussant of Central Secretariat Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year he became a discussant of Central Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 大德元年，除吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dade he was appointed Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In 1297 he was appointed Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 選曹銓注，多有私其鄉里者，元珪曰：「此風不可長，川黨、朔黨之興，宋之所由衰也。

translations.literal: In the selection bureau many favored their own native places in appointments; Yuangui said: "This practice must not be allowed to grow; the rise of Sichuan factions and northern factions was how the Song declined."
translations.idiomatic: In the appointments bureau many officials favored their own home regions. Yuangui warned, "This habit must not be indulged—the rise of regional factions was how the Song dynasty fell into decay."

sentences.zh: 」請謁悉皆謝絕。

translations.literal: " He declined all requests for private audiences.
translations.idiomatic: " He turned away every private petition.

sentences.zh: 三年，宣撫燕南，劾貪吏若干人。

translations.literal: In the third year he was sent to pacify and console Yannan and impeached several corrupt officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was dispatched to pacify Yannan and impeached several corrupt officials.

sentences.zh: 遷工部尚書，河朔連年水旱，五穀不登，元珪言：「《春秋》之義，以養民為本，凡用民力者必書，蓋民力息則生養遂，生養遂則教化行而風俗美。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Works. North of the Yellow River suffered flood and drought year after year and the five grains did not ripen. Yuangui said: "The principle of the Spring and Autumn Annals takes nourishing the people as fundamental; whenever the people's labor is employed it must be recorded—for when the people's strength rests, sustenance and nurture proceed, and when sustenance and nurture proceed, instruction is carried out and customs become fine."
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Minister of Works at a time when the north had suffered flood and drought for years and harvests failed, Yuangui argued: "The Spring and Autumn Annals teach that nourishing the people comes first and that every use of popular labor must be recorded. When the people's strength is spared, they can thrive; when they thrive, education spreads and customs improve."

sentences.zh: 」宰相嘉其言，土木之工稍為之息。

translations.literal: " The chief ministers praised his words, and construction projects were somewhat reduced.
translations.idiomatic: " The chief ministers approved his argument, and construction work was scaled back.

sentences.zh: 六年，僉河南行中書省事，將行，拜江浙行省參知政事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed to sign Henan Branch Secretariat affairs; before departing he was appointed Assistant Administrator of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was appointed to the Henan Branch Secretariat, but before he could leave he was made assistant administrator of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat instead.

sentences.zh: 初，硃清、張瑄以財雄江南，遍以金幣連結當路，及伏誅，錄其家，具籍所交諸公貴人，而江浙省臣為尤甚，惟元珪一無所污。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhu Qing and Zhang Xuan, wealthy lords of the south of the Yangtze, had everywhere linked the powerful with gold and cash; when they were executed their households were inventoried, and registers were made of all the great officials and nobles they had associated with—the Jiang-Zhe provincial ministers were especially implicated, but Yuangui alone was unstained.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhu Qing and Zhang Xuan had dominated Jiangnan through wealth, buying influence with gold and cash throughout the bureaucracy. When they were executed, inventories of their dealings exposed many high officials—especially among the Jiang-Zhe provincial ministers—yet Yuangui alone remained untainted.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，由僉樞密院事拜樞密副使。

translations.literal: When Wuzong took the throne, from signing Bureau of Military Affairs affairs he was appointed Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong came to the throne, Yuangui rose from signing military affairs to vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 詔元珪二十餘人議政中書，若惜人力，嚴選舉，節財用，定律令，謹賞罰，建科舉，課農桑，汰冗員，易封贈，皆切於世務者。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yuangui and more than twenty others to deliberate on government at the Central Secretariat—such matters as sparing human labor, tightening selection, economizing expenditures, fixing laws and statutes, being careful with rewards and punishments, establishing the civil service examinations, supervising agriculture and sericulture, eliminating redundant posts, and reforming enfeoffment and posthumous honors—all pressing on the affairs of the age.
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed Yuangui and more than twenty others to deliberate on state policy at the Central Secretariat—sparing labor, tightening appointments, cutting expenses, fixing laws, disciplining rewards and punishments, restoring examinations, promoting agriculture, eliminating redundant posts, and reforming enfeoffments and posthumous honors—each a matter of urgent public concern.

sentences.zh: 初，詔發軍萬人屯田稱海以實邊，海都之亂，被俘者眾，至是頗有來歸者，飢寒不能存，至鬻子以活。

translations.literal: Earlier an edict had dispatched ten thousand soldiers to garrison fields at Chenghai to strengthen the border; in Haidu's rebellion many were taken captive, and by this time quite a number had returned, but hunger and cold left them unable to survive, even to the point of selling their children to live.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier ten thousand soldiers had been sent to garrison Chenghai and strengthen the frontier. Many had been captured in Haidu's rebellion; now a number were returning home, but hunger and cold drove some to sell their children to survive.

sentences.zh: 元珪具其事以聞，詔賜錢贖之。

translations.literal: Yuangui reported the full circumstances to the throne, and an edict granted money to redeem them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuangui reported the situation in full, and the court issued funds to ransom the children.

sentences.zh: 帝在軍中，即聞元珪名，至是，特加平章政事，賜白金二百五十兩、只孫衣四襲。

translations.literal: While the Emperor was in the army he had already heard Yuangui's name; at this time he was specially advanced to Grand Councillor and bestowed two hundred fifty taels of white silver and four sets of zhisun robes.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had known Yuangui's reputation since his days in the field army; now he was specially promoted to grand councillor and granted two hundred fifty taels of silver and four sets of zhisun robes.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，詔元珪與十六人議時政。

translations.literal: When Renzong took the throne, an edict ordered Yuangui and sixteen others to deliberate on current policy.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong came to the throne, he ordered Yuangui and sixteen others to deliberate on current affairs.

sentences.zh: 皇慶元年，出拜江浙行省左丞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangqing he was sent out to serve as Left Chancellor of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 1312 he was sent out to serve as Left Chancellor of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 江淮漕臣言：「江南殷富，蓋由多匿腴田，若再行檢覆之法，當益田畝累萬計。

translations.literal: The grain transport officials of the Jiang-Huai region said: "The south of the Yangtze is wealthy and abundant, largely because many fertile fields are concealed; if the method of re-inspection and verification were applied again, field acreage would increase by tens of thousands."
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang-Huai grain transport officials argued: "Jiangnan appears prosperous chiefly because many fertile fields are concealed from the registers. If we reinstated field inspections, we could add tens of thousands of acres to the tax rolls."

sentences.zh: 」元珪曰：「江南之平，幾四十年，戶有定籍，田有定畝，一有動搖，其害不細。

translations.literal: " Yuangui said: "The south of the Yangtze has been pacified for nearly forty years; households have fixed registers and fields have fixed acreage—once this is disturbed, the harm will not be slight."
translations.idiomatic: " Yuangui objected: "Jiangnan has been at peace for nearly forty years. Household registers and field acreage are fixed. Disturb them and the harm will be grave."

sentences.zh: 」執其論固爭，月餘不能止，移疾去。

translations.literal: " He held to his view and argued firmly; for more than a month he could not stop it, and he submitted notice of illness and left.
translations.idiomatic: " He held to his position and argued for more than a month without success, then resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 延祐元年，拜甘肅行省左丞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanyou he was appointed Left Chancellor of the Gansu Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 1314 he was appointed Left Chancellor of the Gansu Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，召還，俾宣撫遼陽諸郡，復為樞密副使，召見嘉禧殿，帝曰：「卿先朝舊臣，宜在舊服。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was recalled, made to pacify and console the commanderies of Liaoyang, and again became Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs. Summoned to audience in Jiaxi Hall, the Emperor said: "You are an old minister of the previous reign and ought to resume your former office."
translations.idiomatic: After a little more than a year he was recalled, sent to pacify the commanderies of Liaoyang, and restored as vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs. Received in audience at Jiaxi Hall, the Emperor said, "You are a veteran of the previous reign and belong in your old post."

sentences.zh: 」特加榮祿大夫，賜鈔五千緡、貂裘二襲。

translations.literal: " He was specially advanced to Grand Master for Glorious Blessing and granted five thousand strings of paper money and two sable fur coats.
translations.idiomatic: " He was specially promoted to Grand Master for Glorious Blessing and granted five thousand strings of paper money and two sable coats.

sentences.zh: 元珪奏曰：「昔世祖限田四百畝，以給軍需，餘田悉貢賦稅。

translations.literal: Yuangui memorialized, saying: "Formerly Shizu limited fields to four hundred mu to supply military needs; all remaining fields were to pay tribute and taxes."
translations.idiomatic: Yuangui memorialized: "In Kublai's day fields were capped at four hundred mu for military supply, and all surplus land paid tribute and tax."

sentences.zh: 今經理江淮田土，第以增金為能，加以有司頭會箕斂，俾元元之民，困苦日甚，臣恐變生不測，非國之福，惟陛下少加意焉。

translations.literal: Now in managing the fields and lands of the Jiang-Huai region, merit is measured solely by increasing revenue; moreover the officials scrape together levies with combs and rakes, so that the common people grow daily more distressed. I fear unforeseen disturbances may arise—this is not a blessing to the state. I beg Your Majesty to give this a little attention.
translations.idiomatic: Today officials managing Jiang-Huai land are praised only for raising revenue, while local officers squeeze the people with every levy. The common folk grow more wretched by the day. I fear unrest may follow—this cannot benefit the state. I beg your Majesty to take heed.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「凡爾軍士之田，並遵舊制。」

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "As for all fields belonging to soldiers, let the old regulations be followed throughout."
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor replied, "All land held by soldiers shall follow the old regulations."

sentences.zh: 至治元年，英宗即位，元珪與知樞密院事帖木兒不花上軍民之政十餘事，大抵言：諸王近侍，不可干軍政；

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhizhi, when Yingzong took the throne, Yuangui together with Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Temür Buqa presented more than ten items on military and civil administration, broadly stating: princes and court favorites must not interfere in military affairs;
translations.idiomatic: In 1321, when Yingzong came to the throne, Yuangui and Director Temür Buqa submitted more than ten recommendations on military and civil administration, chief among them that princes and court favorites must not meddle in military affairs;

sentences.zh: 管軍官吏，不可漁取軍戶；

translations.literal: officers who administer troops must not prey upon military households;
translations.idiomatic: officers administering troops must not prey on military households;

sentences.zh: 軍官之材者，當遷其職；

translations.literal: military officers of talent should be transferred to suitable posts;
translations.idiomatic: talented officers should be reassigned to posts suited to their abilities;

sentences.zh: 有司賦役，當務均一，而軍民不可有所偏；

translations.literal: official levies and corvée labor should strive for uniformity, and neither military nor civilian populations should be favored;
translations.idiomatic: taxes and corvée must be applied evenly, with no favor shown to either soldiers or civilians;

sentences.zh: 軍官襲職，惟傳嫡嗣，而支庶不可有所亂。

translations.literal: inheriting military office should pass only to legitimate heirs of the direct line, and collateral branches must not be allowed to cause disorder.
translations.idiomatic: hereditary military posts should pass only to legitimate heirs of the main line, and collateral kin must not be allowed to disrupt succession.

sentences.zh: 帝並嘉納，即降旨施行之。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved all and immediately issued edicts to put them into effect.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved every recommendation and immediately issued edicts to carry them out.

sentences.zh: 元珪以年老致仕，至治二年，起商議中書省事。

translations.literal: Yuangui retired on account of age; in the second year of Zhizhi he was recalled to deliberate on Central Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yuangui had retired on grounds of age, but in 1322 he was recalled to deliberate on Central Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 三年卒。

translations.literal: In the third year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of the reign.

sentences.zh: 泰定元年，贈光祿大夫、河南等處行省平章政事、柱國，追封趙國公，諡忠簡。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiding he was posthumously granted Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Grand Councillor of the Henan Branch Secretariat, and Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao, with the posthumous name Zhongjian.
translations.idiomatic: In 1324 he was posthumously honored as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and Grand Councillor of the Henan Branch Secretariat, enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao, with the posthumous name Zhongjian, "Loyal and Simple."

sentences.zh: 三年，復加推誠佐理功臣、光祿大夫、司徒。

translations.literal: In the third year he was further granted the title Meritorious Subject Who Sincerely Assists Governance, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he received the additional honors of meritorious subject who sincerely assisted governance, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: ○張昇

translations.literal: ○ Zhang Sheng
translations.idiomatic: ○ Zhang Sheng

sentences.zh: 張昇，字伯高，其先定州人，後徙平州。

translations.literal: Zhang Sheng, courtesy name Bogao, his ancestors were from Dingzhou and later moved to Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Sheng, whose courtesy name was Bogao, came from a family originally of Dingzhou that later moved to Pingzhou.

sentences.zh: 升幼警敏過人，學語時，輒能辨字音，應對異於常兒；

translations.literal: Sheng as a child was alert and clever beyond others; when learning to speak he could distinguish character pronunciations, and his replies differed from ordinary children;
translations.idiomatic: As a child Sheng was unusually quick-witted; even while learning to speak he could distinguish character sounds, and his replies were unlike those of other children;

sentences.zh: 既長，力學，工文辭。

translations.literal: when he grew up he studied diligently and was skilled in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: when he grew older he studied hard and became accomplished in literary composition.

sentences.zh: 至元二十九年，用薦者授將仕郎、翰林國史院編修官，預修《世祖實錄》。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Zhiyuan, through a recommender he was appointed Gentleman-in-Attendance and Compiler in the Hanlin Academy National History Office, participating in the compilation of the Veritable Records of Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1292, on recommendation, he was appointed Gentleman-in-Attendance and compiler in the Hanlin Academy's National History Office, where he helped compile the 《Veritable Records of Kublai》.

sentences.zh: 升應奉翰林文字，尋升修撰，歷興文署令，遷太常博士。

translations.literal: Sheng served as Hanlin Attendant for Composition, was soon promoted to Compiler, served as Director of the Office for the Promotion of Literature, and was transferred to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng served as Hanlin attendant for composition, was soon promoted to compiler, became director of the Office for the Promotion of Literature, and was then transferred to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 成宗崩，大臣承中旨，議奉徽號，饗宗廟，升曰：「在故典，凡有事於宗廟，必書嗣皇帝名，今將何書？

translations.literal: When Chengzong died, the great ministers, acting on an inner edict, deliberated on bestowing a posthumous honorific title and offering sacrifices at the ancestral temple. Sheng said: "In the old statutes, whenever there is an affair at the ancestral temple, the name of the succeeding emperor must be written—what name shall be written now?"
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzong died, the chief ministers, acting on a secret edict, debated posthumous honors and ancestral sacrifices. Sheng asked, "According to precedent, any ancestral temple rite must record the succeeding emperor's name—whose name should be entered now?"

sentences.zh: 」議遂寢。

translations.literal: " The deliberation was thereupon dropped.
translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，議躬祀禮，升據經引古，參酌時宜以對，帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: When Wuzong took the throne, they deliberated on the rites of personal sacrifice. Sheng cited the classics and ancient precedents, weighing present circumstances in his reply, and the Emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong came to the throne, the court debated the rites of personal sacrifice. Sheng answered by citing the classics and ancient precedent while adapting them to present needs, and the Emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 至大初，改太常寺為太常禮儀院，即除升為判官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhida the Court of Imperial Sacrifices was changed to the Court of Imperial Sacrificial Rites, and Sheng was immediately appointed its Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhida reign the Court of Imperial Sacrifices was reorganized as the Court of Imperial Sacrificial Rites, and Sheng was appointed its vice director.

sentences.zh: 久之，外補知汝寧府。

translations.literal: After a long while he was sent out to serve as Prefect of Runing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was posted outside the capital as prefect of Runing.

sentences.zh: 民有告寄束書於其家者，逾三年取閱，有禁書一編，且記里中大家姓名於上，升亟呼吏焚其書，曰：「妄言誣民，且再更赦矣，勿論。

translations.literal: A commoner reported that someone had left a bundle of books at his home; after more than three years he took them out to read them and found one volume of prohibited books, with the names of leading families in the neighborhood recorded upon it. Sheng immediately called clerks to burn the book, saying: "This is false speech to slander the people, and moreover there have been two general amnesties since—do not pursue the matter."
translations.idiomatic: A man reported that someone had left a bundle of books at his house. More than three years later he opened it and found a volume of banned books listing the names of prominent local families. Sheng immediately ordered the book burned, saying, "This is a false accusation against innocent people, and two general amnesties have passed since—let the matter drop."

sentences.zh: 」同列懼，皆引起。

translations.literal: " His colleagues were afraid and all rose to leave.
translations.idiomatic: " His colleagues were alarmed and all rose to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 既而事聞，廷議謂升脫姦軌，遣使窮問，卒無跡可指，乃詰以擅焚書狀，升對曰：「事固類姦軌，然升備位郡守，為民父母，今斥誣訴，免冤濫，雖重得罪不避。

translations.literal: When the matter became known, court deliberation held that Sheng had shielded treasonous conduct and dispatched envoys to investigate thoroughly; in the end no trace could be pointed to. They then questioned him for burning the book on his own authority. Sheng replied: "The matter indeed resembles treasonous conduct, yet Sheng holds the post of prefect and is parent to the people; now to reject false accusations and spare wrongful punishment—even if I incur serious guilt I will not shrink from it."
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the capital, the court suspected Sheng of shielding sedition and sent investigators, but they found no evidence. He was then charged with burning the book without authorization. Sheng replied, "The case did look like sedition, but as prefect I am parent to the people. I rejected a false accusation to spare innocent suffering, and I would not shrink from punishment for that."

sentences.zh: 」乃坐奪俸二月。

translations.literal: " He was therefore sentenced to forfeiture of salary for two months.
translations.idiomatic: " He was sentenced to two months' forfeiture of salary.

sentences.zh: 旁郡移文報吳人侯君遠者言：「歲直壬子六月朔日蝕，其占為兵寇；

translations.literal: A neighboring prefecture sent an official dispatch reporting that a man of Wu named Hou Junyuan said: "In the year of the renzi cycle, on the first day of the sixth month there will be an eclipse; the omen is military invasion;"
translations.idiomatic: A neighboring prefecture forwarded a report that a man of Wu named Hou Junyuan had declared: "In the renzi year, on the first day of the sixth month there will be an eclipse, and the omen foretells war;"

sentences.zh: 歲癸丑，其應在吳分野。

translations.literal: "in the guichou year the fulfillment will fall in the Wu astral domain."
translations.idiomatic: "in the following guichou year the omen will fall upon the Wu region."

sentences.zh: 」同列欲召屬縣為備禦計，升曰：「此訛言，久當自息，毋用惑民聽。

translations.literal: " His colleagues wished to summon the subordinate counties to make defensive preparations. Sheng said: "This is false rumor; in time it will die away of itself—there is no need to alarm the people."
translations.idiomatic: " His colleagues wanted to summon the subordinate counties to prepare defenses. Sheng said, "This is mere rumor; it will die away on its own—do not alarm the people."

sentences.zh: 」斥其無稽，眾論韙之。

translations.literal: " He rejected it as groundless, and public opinion approved him.
translations.idiomatic: " He dismissed it as baseless, and his colleagues agreed.

sentences.zh: 部使者舉治行為諸郡最。

translations.literal: The ministry envoy cited his governance as the best among all prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry inspector ranked his administration the finest among the prefectures.

sentences.zh: 歷江西行省左右司郎中，除紹興路總管。

translations.literal: He served as Director of the Left and Right Secretariats of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat and was appointed Circuit Intendant of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: He served as director in the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat and was appointed circuit intendant of Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 初，大德、至大間，越大饑，且疫癘，民死者殆半，賦稅鹽課責里胥代納，吏並緣為奸，害富家，升為證於簿籍，白行省蠲之。

translations.literal: Earlier, between Dade and Zhida, Yue suffered great famine and pestilence as well; nearly half the people died. Taxes and salt levies were charged to village headmen to pay on behalf of others, and clerks used the opportunity for corruption, harming wealthy families. Sheng verified this against the registers and reported to the Branch Secretariat to remit them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Dade and Zhida reigns, Shaoxing had suffered severe famine and plague, and nearly half the population perished. Tax and salt obligations were forced onto village headmen, while clerks used the crisis to extort wealthy families. Sheng documented the abuses in the registers and persuaded the Branch Secretariat to remit the levies.

sentences.zh: 前守有為江浙行省參知政事者，爭代者祿米，有隙，欲內之罪，移平江歲輸海運糧布囊三萬，俾紹興制如數，民患苦之，不能堪。

translations.literal: A former prefect who had become Assistant Administrator of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat disputed with Sheng over substitute grain salaries and bore a grudge, wishing to entrap him in guilt. He shifted to Shaoxing the annual maritime transport quota of thirty thousand sacks of grain and cloth from Pingjiang, requiring Shaoxing to supply the same amount; the people suffered bitterly and could not endure it.
translations.idiomatic: A former prefect who had risen to assistant administrator of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat quarreled with Sheng over substitute grain salaries and sought to trap him. He shifted Pingjiang's annual maritime transport quota of thirty thousand sacks of grain and cloth onto Shaoxing, and the people could not bear the burden.

sentences.zh: 更數守，謂歲例如此，置弗問。

translations.literal: After several successive prefects, they said this was the annual precedent and left it unaddressed.
translations.idiomatic: Several successive prefects accepted it as annual precedent and ignored the problem.

sentences.zh: 升言：「麻非越土所生，海漕實吳郡事，於越無與。

translations.literal: Sheng said: "Hemp is not produced in Yue soil; maritime transport is truly a matter of the Wu commanderies and has nothing to do with Yue."
translations.idiomatic: Sheng argued, "Hemp is not produced in Yue, and maritime transport is truly a Wu responsibility—Shaoxing should have no part in it."

sentences.zh: 」章上，卒罷之。

translations.literal: " When his memorial went up, the levy was finally abolished.
translations.idiomatic: " His memorial prevailed, and the levy was abolished.

sentences.zh: 升既謹於繩吏，又果於去民瘼，故人心悅服。

translations.literal: Sheng was both strict in restraining clerks and resolute in removing the people's afflictions, so the people's hearts were pleased and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was strict with officials and resolute in removing the people's burdens, and the people came to trust him wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 歷湖北道廉訪使、江南行台治書侍御史，召為參議中書省事，改樞密院判官，尋復中書參議。

translations.literal: He served as Surveillance Commissioner of the Hubei Circuit, Investigating Censor and Attendant Censor of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate, was summoned as Discussant of Central Secretariat Affairs, was changed to Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and soon returned to Secretariat Discussant.
translations.idiomatic: He served as surveillance commissioner of the Hubei circuit and investigating censor on the Jiangnan Branch Censorate, was recalled as a Central Secretariat discussant, became vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and soon returned to Secretariat discussant.

sentences.zh: 至治二年，又出為河東道廉訪使，未行，拜治書侍御史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhizhi he was again sent out as Surveillance Commissioner of the Hedong Circuit; before departing he was appointed Investigating Censor and Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1322 he was posted as surveillance commissioner of the Hedong circuit, but before he could leave he was appointed investigating censor and attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 明年，出為淮西道廉訪使。

translations.literal: The next year he was sent out as Surveillance Commissioner of the Huaixi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was posted as surveillance commissioner of the Huaixi circuit.

sentences.zh: 泰定二年，拜陝西行省參知政事，加中奉大夫，尋遷遼東道廉訪使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiding he was appointed Assistant Administrator of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat and advanced to Grand Master for Fostering Integrity; soon he was transferred to Surveillance Commissioner of the Liaodong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1325 he was appointed assistant administrator of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat and promoted to Grand Master for Fostering Integrity, then transferred to surveillance commissioner of the Liaodong circuit.

sentences.zh: 屬永平大水，民多捐瘠，升請發海道糧十八萬石、鈔五萬緡，以賑饑民，且蠲其歲賦，朝廷從之，民得全活者眾。

translations.literal: When Yongping suffered great flood, many of the people were emaciated. Sheng requested the release of one hundred eighty thousand piculs of maritime transport grain and fifty thousand strings of paper money to relieve the starving people, and moreover remission of their annual levies. The court assented, and many people were thereby preserved alive.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongping was struck by severe flooding and many people were starving, Sheng requested one hundred eighty thousand piculs of maritime grain and fifty thousand strings of paper money for relief, along with remission of annual taxes. The court approved, and countless lives were saved.

sentences.zh: 明年，召拜侍御史。

translations.literal: The next year he was summoned and appointed Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was recalled and appointed attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 天歷初，出為山東道廉訪使，時方有警，有司請完城以為備，升曰：「民恃吾以生，完城是棄民也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianli he was sent out as Surveillance Commissioner of the Shandong Circuit. There was then an alarm, and the officials requested repairing the city walls for defense. Sheng said: "The people rely on me for their livelihood; to repair the walls is to abandon the people."
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianli reign he was posted as surveillance commissioner of the Shandong circuit. When unrest threatened, officials proposed repairing the city walls. Sheng objected, "The people depend on me for their livelihood—fortifying the walls means abandoning them."

sentences.zh: 」由是民皆安之。

translations.literal: " Thereby the people were all reassured.
translations.idiomatic: " The people were thereby reassured.

sentences.zh: 文宗賜尚醖文幣，以賞其功。

translations.literal: Wenzong bestowed imperial wine and patterned silks to reward his merit.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong rewarded him with imperial wine and patterned silks.

sentences.zh: 逾年，召為太禧院副使，兼奉贊神御殿事，除河南省左丞，复遷淮西道廉訪使。

translations.literal: After a year he was summoned as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Blessings, concurrently attending to the Divine Imperial Hall, appointed Left Chancellor of the Henan Province Secretariat, and again transferred to Surveillance Commissioner of the Huaixi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was recalled as vice director of the Court of Imperial Blessings with duties at the Divine Imperial Hall, appointed Left Chancellor of Henan, and again transferred to surveillance commissioner of the Huaixi circuit.

sentences.zh: 升時年六十有九，上書乞致仕。

translations.literal: Sheng was then sixty-nine years old and submitted a memorial requesting retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was then sixty-nine and submitted a memorial requesting retirement.

sentences.zh: 至順二年，復起為集賢侍講學士，文宗眷待之意甚隆。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhishun he was again raised to Lecturing Academician of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies; Wenzong's favor toward him was very great.
translations.idiomatic: In 1331 he was recalled as lecturing academician of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, and Wenzong treated him with exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 元統元年，順帝即位，首詔在廷耆艾，訪問治道，升條上時所宜先者十事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuantong, when Shundi took the throne, the first edict summoned the elders at court to inquire about the way of governance; Sheng itemized ten matters that should be prioritized at the time.
translations.idiomatic: In 1333, when Shundi came to the throne, his first edict summoned the elders at court to advise on governance. Sheng submitted ten priorities for the age.

sentences.zh: 尋兼經筵官，廷試進士，特命升讀卷，事已，告省先墓。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made an instructor at the Classics Colloquium; at the palace examination for jinshi he was specially ordered to read the examination papers. When the affair was finished, he requested leave to visit his ancestors' tombs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made an instructor at the Classics Colloquium and was specially ordered to read examination papers at the palace jinshi examination. When the examinations ended, he asked leave to visit his family's graves.

sentences.zh: 帝賜金織文袍，以寵其歸。

translations.literal: The Emperor bestowed a gold-woven patterned robe to honor his departure.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor granted him a gold-woven ceremonial robe to honor his journey home.

sentences.zh: 明年，以奎章閣大學士、資善大夫、知經筵事召，賜上尊，趣就職，升以疾辭。

translations.literal: The next year he was summoned as Grand Academician of the Kuizhang Pavilion, Grand Master for Assisting Goodness, and Director of Classics Colloquium Affairs; fine wine was bestowed and he was urged to take office, but Sheng declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was summoned as grand academician of the Kuizhang Pavilion and director of the Classics Colloquium, with fine wine sent to hurry him to office, but Sheng declined on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 帝察其不可強，許之。

translations.literal: The Emperor perceived he could not be compelled and granted permission.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that he could not be pressed, the Emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 尋命本郡月給祿半，以終其身。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to receive half salary monthly from his home prefecture for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon granted half his former salary monthly from his home prefecture for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 至正元年卒，年八十一。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhizheng he died, aged eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1341 at the age of eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈資德大夫、河南等處行中書省左丞，諡文憲。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted Grand Master for Assisting Virtue and Left Chancellor of the Henan Branch Secretariat, with the posthumous name Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Master for Assisting Virtue and Left Chancellor of the Henan Branch Secretariat, with the posthumous name Wenxian, "Cultured and Lawful."

sentences.zh: 臧夢解陸垕

translations.literal: Zang Mengjie and Lu Hou
translations.idiomatic: Zang Mengjie and Lu Hou

sentences.zh: 臧夢解，慶元人，宋末中進士第，未官而國亡。

translations.literal: Zang Mengjie was a man of Qingyuan; at the end of the Song he passed the jinshi examination but had not yet taken office when the state perished.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Mengjie was a native of Qingyuan. He passed the jinshi examination at the end of the Song dynasty but never took office before the dynasty fell.

sentences.zh: 至元十三年，從其鄉郡守將內附，授奉訓大夫、婺州路軍民人匠提舉。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhiyuan he followed his home prefecture's commandery prefect in submitting to the dynasty and was appointed Grand Master for Fostering Instruction and Superintendent of Military and Civil Artisans of Wuzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1276 he followed his home prefect in submitting to the Yuan and was appointed Grand Master for Fostering Instruction and superintendent of military and civil artisans in Wuzhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 未幾，例革其所司，而浙東宣慰司舉夢解才兼儒吏，可試州郡，朝廷是之，授息州知州。

translations.literal: Before long, by regulation his office was abolished, but the Zhedong Pacification Commission recommended that Mengjie combined talent as both scholar and administrator and could be tried in prefecture and commandery posts; the court approved and appointed him Prefect of Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward his office was abolished by regulation, but the Zhedong Pacification Commission recommended him as a man combining scholarly and administrative talent fit for prefectural service. The court agreed and appointed him prefect of Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 未行，改知海寧州。

translations.literal: Before departing he was changed to Prefect of Haining Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post he was reassigned as prefect of Haining.

sentences.zh: 時淮東按察副使王慶之按行至其州，見夢解剛直廉慎，而學有淵奧，自任職以來，門無私謁，官署蕭然，凡有差役，皆當其貧富，而吏無所預。

translations.literal: At that time Vice Surveillance Commissioner Wang Qingzhi of Huaidong conducted an inspection tour to his prefecture and saw that Mengjie was upright, incorruptible, and cautious, with learning of profound depth. Since taking office there had been no private audiences at his gate, and the government offices were austere; whenever there were corvée assignments, all were assessed according to wealth and poverty, and clerks had no part in it.
translations.idiomatic: When Vice Surveillance Commissioner Wang Qingzhi of Huaidong inspected Haining, he found Mengjie upright, incorruptible, and learned in the deepest sense. Since taking office Mengjie had admitted no private callers, kept his offices austere, assessed every corvée levy according to each household's means, and allowed no clerk to interfere.

sentences.zh: 於是民以戶計者，新增七百六十有四；

translations.literal: thereupon households registered among the people increased by seven hundred sixty-four;
translations.idiomatic: Registered households increased by seven hundred sixty-four;

sentences.zh: 田以頃計者，新辟四百四十有三；

translations.literal: fields reckoned in qing newly opened amounted to four hundred forty-three;
translations.idiomatic: newly opened fields totaled four hundred forty-three qing;

sentences.zh: 桑柘榆柳，交廕境內，而政平訟簡，為諸州縣最。

translations.literal: mulberry, catalpa, elm, and willow shaded one another within the borders, while government was peaceful and litigation few—he was foremost among all prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: mulberry, catalpa, elm, and willow trees shaded the countryside, government was peaceful, litigation was rare, and his prefecture ranked first among all counties.

sentences.zh: 乃舉夢解才德兼備，宜擢清要，以展所蘊。

translations.literal: He therefore recommended that Mengjie combined talent and virtue and ought to be promoted to a lofty and important post to display what he contained.
translations.idiomatic: Wang therefore recommended that Mengjie, combining talent and virtue, deserved promotion to a high post where his abilities could be fully used.

sentences.zh: 而御史臺亦以其廉能，抗章薦之。

translations.literal: The Censorate also, for his integrity and ability, submitted a forthright memorial recommending him.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate likewise submitted a memorial recommending him for his integrity and competence.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，夢解滿去者至是已五年矣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, five years had passed since Mengjie's term had expired and he had left office.
translations.idiomatic: By the twenty-seventh year, five years had passed since Mengjie completed his term and left office.

sentences.zh: 屬江陰飢，江浙行省委夢解賑之。

translations.literal: When Jiangyin suffered famine, the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat commissioned Mengjie to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangyin suffered famine, the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat commissioned Mengjie to administer relief.

sentences.zh: 夢解不為文具，皆躬至其地，而人給以米，所活四萬五千餘人。

translations.literal: Mengjie did not make mere documents; he personally went to every place and gave each person rice, preserving alive more than forty-five thousand people.
translations.idiomatic: Mengjie dispensed with paperwork, went personally to every affected place, and distributed rice to each person, saving more than forty-five thousand lives.

sentences.zh: 江南行台治書侍御史苟宗道，聞而韙之，舉其名上聞，除同知桂陽路總管府事。

translations.literal: Gou Zongdao, Investigating Censor and Attendant Censor of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate, heard of this and approved, reporting his name to the throne; Mengjie was appointed Associate Administrator of the Guiyang Circuit Intendant's Office.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Zongdao, investigating censor on the Jiangnan Branch Censorate, heard of his work and approved, reporting his name to the throne. Mengjie was appointed associate administrator of the Guiyang circuit intendant's office.

sentences.zh: 三十年，擢奉議大夫、廣西肅政廉訪副使。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he was promoted to Grand Master for Discussion and Vice Surveillance Commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year he was promoted to Grand Master for Discussion and vice surveillance commissioner of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 故事，煙瘴之地，行部者多不躬至，而夢解咸遍歷焉。

translations.literal: By precedent, in miasmal regions those conducting inspection tours often did not go in person, but Mengjie visited them all.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, inspectors rarely visited miasmal regions in person, but Mengjie toured every one of them himself.

sentences.zh: 遂按問賓州、藤州兩路達魯花赤，與凡貪官姦吏，置於法者無慮八十餘人。

translations.literal: He thereupon investigated the darughachi of the Binzhou and Tengzhou circuits and all corrupt and treacherous officials; those punished by law numbered no fewer than eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He investigated the darughachi of Binzhou and Tengzhou circuits and every corrupt official he found, punishing no fewer than eighty men by law.

sentences.zh: 又平反邕州黃震被誣贓罪，及藤州唐氏婦被誣殺夫罪，凡兩冤獄。

translations.literal: He also redressed two wrongful cases: Huang Zhen of Yongzhou falsely accused of embezzlement, and a woman of the Tang family in Tengzhou falsely accused of murdering her husband.
translations.idiomatic: He also overturned two wrongful convictions: Huang Zhen of Yongzhou, falsely accused of embezzlement, and a Mrs. Tang of Tengzhou, falsely accused of murdering her husband.

sentences.zh: 大德元年，遷江西肅政廉訪副使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dade he was transferred to Vice Surveillance Commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1297 he was transferred to vice surveillance commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 有臨江路總管李倜，素狡獪，而又附大臣勢，以控持省憲，夢解按其贓罪，而一道澄清。

translations.literal: There was Circuit Intendant Li Ti of Linjiang, by nature cunning and deceitful, who moreover relied on the power of great ministers to control the provincial censorate. Mengjie investigated his crimes of embezzlement, and the whole circuit was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: The circuit intendant Li Ti of Linjiang was notoriously cunning and used powerful patrons to intimidate the provincial censorate. Mengjie prosecuted him for embezzlement and restored integrity throughout the circuit.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷浙東肅政廉訪副使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Vice Surveillance Commissioner of Zhedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was transferred to vice surveillance commissioner of Zhedong.

sentences.zh: 九年，除廣東肅政廉訪使。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed Surveillance Commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was appointed surveillance commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 夢解至是，既老且病，乃納祿退居杭州，以亞中大夫、湖南宣慰副使致仕。

translations.literal: By this time Mengjie was both old and ill; he surrendered his salary and retired to Hangzhou, retiring with the ranks of Subordinate Grand Master and Vice Pacification Commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: By then Mengjie was old and ill. He surrendered his salary and retired to Hangzhou with the honorary ranks of Subordinate Grand Master and Vice Pacification Commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 後至元元年卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Later Zhiyuan he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of the Later Zhiyuan reign.

sentences.zh: 夢解博學洽聞，為時名儒，然不少迂腐，而敏於政事，其操守尤為介特。

translations.literal: Mengjie was broadly learned and well informed, a famous Confucian of the age, yet not at all pedantic; he was keen in government affairs, and his integrity was especially uncompromising.
translations.idiomatic: Mengjie was broadly learned and widely informed, a celebrated scholar of his day, yet not pedantic; he was sharp in administration, and his integrity was exceptionally uncompromising.

sentences.zh: 所著書，有《周官考》三卷、《春秋微》一卷。

translations.literal: Among his written works were three juan of Examination of the Offices of Zhou and one juan of Subtleties of the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: His writings included three juan of 《Examination of the Offices of Zhou》 and one juan of 《Subtleties of the Spring and Autumn Annals》.

sentences.zh: 夢解嘗自號魯山大夫，士之稱之者，不以官，皆曰魯山先生云。

translations.literal: Mengjie once styled himself the Grandee of Lushan; scholars who spoke of him did not use his office title but all called him Master Lushan.
translations.idiomatic: Mengjie styled himself the Grandee of Lushan, and scholars spoke of him not by his official title but as Master Lushan.

sentences.zh: 同時有陸垕者，與夢解齊名。

translations.literal: At the same time there was Lu Hou, equally famous with Mengjie.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time there was Lu Hou, who enjoyed equal renown with Mengjie.

sentences.zh: 監察御史鄭鵬南嘗以二人並薦於朝。

translations.literal: Investigating Censor Zheng Pengnan once recommended the two men together to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censor Zheng Pengnan once recommended both men together to the court.

sentences.zh: 垕字仁重，江陰人也。

translations.literal: Hou, courtesy name Renzhong, was a man of Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Hou, whose courtesy name was Renzhong, was a native of Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 自幼以孝友聞。

translations.literal: From childhood he was known for filial piety and brotherly affection.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he was known for filial piety and devotion to his brothers.

sentences.zh: 至元間，丞相伯顏以師南下，垕是時年未冠，而志強氣銳，率其鄉人見之，論議有合，兵遂不涉其境，鄉人義之。

translations.literal: During Zhiyuan, Chancellor Bayan led the army south. Hou was then not yet capped in age, yet his will was strong and his spirit keen; he led the people of his township to see him. Their discussion accorded, and the army therefore did not enter his territory; the townspeople honored his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhiyuan era, Chancellor Bayan marched south with his army. Hou was not yet twenty, yet bold and resolute; he led his townspeople to meet Bayan. Their discussion agreed, and the army did not enter his district. The people honored his courage.

sentences.zh: 伯顏奏授為同知徽州路總管府事，以廉能擢置台憲，累遷至湖南肅政廉訪副使，升浙西廉訪使。

translations.literal: Bayan memorialized to appoint him Associate Administrator of the Huizhou Circuit Intendant's Office; for integrity and ability he was promoted into the censorate, rising through successive transfers to Vice Surveillance Commissioner of Hunan and then Surveillance Commissioner of Zhexi.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan recommended him as associate administrator of the Huizhou circuit intendant's office. For integrity and ability he entered the censorate, rising to vice surveillance commissioner of Hunan and then surveillance commissioner of Zhexi.

sentences.zh: 所至以黜贓吏、洗冤獄為己任，且嘗上章奏免儒役，及舉行浙西助役法。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he took dismissing corrupt officials and clearing wrongful cases as his charge, and he once submitted a memorial requesting exemption of scholars from corvée labor and the implementation of the Zhexi corvée-assistance law.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he made it his mission to dismiss corrupt officials and overturn wrongful convictions. He once memorialized to exempt scholars from corvée labor and to implement the Zhexi corvée-assistance law.

sentences.zh: 年五十卒，賜諡莊簡。

translations.literal: He died at age fifty and was granted the posthumous name Zhuangjian.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty and was granted the posthumous name Zhuangjian, "Solemn and Simple."

sentences.zh: 陳顥，字仲明，其先居盧龍，有名山者，仕金為謀克監軍，太祖得之，以為平陽等路軍民都元帥，子孫徙清州，遂為清州人。

translations.literal: Chen Hao, courtesy name Zhongming, his ancestors dwelt in Lulong; one named Mingshan served the Jin as a mukun military supervisor. Taizu obtained him and made him Commander-in-Chief of Military and Civil Affairs of the Pingyang Circuit and other circuits; his descendants moved to Qingzhou and thus became men of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hao, whose courtesy name was Zhongming, came from a family originally of Lulong. An ancestor named Mingshan had served the Jin as a mukun military supervisor until Taizu took him into service and appointed him commander-in-chief of military and civil affairs for Pingyang and other circuits. His descendants later moved to Qingzhou and became natives of that place.

sentences.zh: 顥幼穎悟，日記誦千百言，稍長，遊京師，登翰林承旨王磐、安藏之門。

translations.literal: Hao as a child was quick-witted; each day he could memorize and recite a thousand or more words. When he grew somewhat older he traveled to the capital and entered the schools of Hanlin Academician-in-Chief Wang Pan and Ancang.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was precocious as a child and could memorize a thousand or more characters a day. When he grew older he went to the capital and studied under the Hanlin academicians Wang Pan and Ancang.

sentences.zh: 磐熟金典章，安藏通諸國語，顥兼習之。

translations.literal: Wang Pan was versed in Jin statutes and regulations; Ancang was proficient in the languages of various states; Hao studied both.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pan was expert in Jin law and institutions; Ancang was fluent in the languages of many peoples; Hao studied both.

sentences.zh: 安藏乃薦顥入宿衛，尋為仁宗潛邸說書。

translations.literal: Ancang thereupon recommended Hao for service in the palace guard, and soon he became lecturer for Renzong's hidden residence.
translations.idiomatic: Ancang recommended Hao for palace guard service, and he soon became lecturer to Renzong while the latter was still heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 於是，仁宗奉母后出居懷慶，顥從行，日開陳以古聖賢居艱貞之道。

translations.literal: Thereupon Renzong, attending the empress dowager, went out to reside at Huaiqing; Hao accompanied him and daily expounded the way ancient sages and worthies maintained steadfast integrity in times of hardship.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong accompanied the empress dowager to reside at Huaiqing, Hao went with him and daily expounded how the ancient sages had upheld steadfast integrity in times of adversity.

sentences.zh: 會成宗崩，仁宗入定內難，以迎武宗，顥皆預謀。

translations.literal: When Chengzong died, Renzong entered the capital during the inner turmoil to welcome Wuzong; Hao took part in all the planning.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzong died, Renzong entered the capital amid the succession crisis to welcome Wuzong, and Hao took part in the planning throughout.

sentences.zh: 及仁宗即位，以推戴舊勳，特拜集賢大學士、榮祿大夫，仍宿衛禁中，政事無不與聞。

translations.literal: When Renzong took the throne, in recognition of his old merit in supporting the enthronement, Hao was specially appointed Grand Academician of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies and Grand Master for Glorious Blessing, still serving in the palace guard within the forbidden precincts; in government affairs there was nothing he did not hear.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong came to the throne, Hao was specially honored for his early support with appointment as grand academician of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies and Grand Master for Glorious Blessing, while continuing to serve in the palace guard. No affair of state escaped his counsel.

sentences.zh: 科舉之行，顥贊助之力尤多。

translations.literal: When the civil service examinations were instituted, Hao's assisting effort was especially great.
translations.idiomatic: When the civil service examinations were restored, Hao's support was especially decisive.

sentences.zh: 顥時伺帝燕閒，輒取聖經所載大經大法有切治體者陳之，每見嘉納。

translations.literal: When Hao observed the Emperor at leisure, he would take from the sacred classics the great principles and fundamental laws bearing on governance and present them; each time he was praised and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he found the Emperor at leisure, Hao would draw from the classics those great principles of governance most relevant to the times, and the Emperor invariably approved.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗坐便殿，群臣入奏事，望見顥，喜曰：「陳仲明在列，所奏必善事矣。
