translations.literal: The Emperor once sat in the informal hall; when the ministers entered to report affairs and saw Hao, he said with pleasure: "With Chen Zhongming present, what is reported must be good counsel."
translations.idiomatic: Once, as ministers came before the Emperor in the informal hall, he saw Hao and said with pleasure, "With Chen Zhongming here, whatever is reported must be sound advice."

sentences.zh: 」顥以父年老，力請歸養清州，帝特命顥長子孝伯為知州以就養。

translations.literal: " Hao, because his father was old, earnestly requested to return to Qingzhou to support him in retirement; the Emperor specially ordered Hao's eldest son Xiaobo to be made Prefect so that he might attend to his father's care.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao, whose father was elderly, begged leave to return to Qingzhou to care for him. The Emperor specially appointed Hao's eldest son Xiaobo prefect of Qingzhou so that the father might be supported in comfort.

sentences.zh: 顥固辭，乃以孝伯為州判官。

translations.literal: Hao firmly declined, and Xiaobo was therefore made Vice Prefect of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Hao declined firmly, and Xiaobo was instead made vice prefect.

sentences.zh: 帝欲用顥為中書平章政事，顥叩首謝曰：「臣無汗馬之功，又乏經濟之略，一旦置之政途，徒速臣咎。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to employ Hao as Grand Councillor of the Central Secretariat; Hao bowed his head and declined, saying: "Your servant has no merit earned in battle, and moreover lacks a strategy for ordering the state; to place me suddenly on the path of government would only hasten my guilt."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wished to appoint Hao grand councillor of the Central Secretariat. Hao bowed and declined: "I have won no merit in battle and lack the capacity to govern the realm. To place me suddenly in high office would only hasten my downfall."

sentences.zh: 臣願得朝夕左右，獻替可否，庶少裨萬一，亦以全臣愚忠。

translations.literal: "Your servant wishes to attend at your side morning and evening, offering approval or rejection, that I may in some small measure be of benefit, and also thereby preserve my foolish loyalty intact."
translations.idiomatic: "I ask only to attend your Majesty morning and evening, offering counsel when needed, that I may serve in some small way and preserve my loyalty unblemished."

sentences.zh: 」帝乃允。

translations.literal: " The Emperor thereupon consented.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 仁宗崩，辭祿家居者十年。

translations.literal: When Renzong died, he resigned his salary and lived at home for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong died, he resigned his salary and lived in retirement at home for ten years.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，復起為集賢大學士，上疏勸帝大興文治、增國子學弟子員、蠲儒之徭役，文宗皆嘉納焉。

translations.literal: When Wenzong took the throne, he was again raised to Grand Academician of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies; he submitted a memorial urging the Emperor to greatly promote literary governance, increase the number of students in the Imperial University, and remit the corvée labor of scholars—all of which Wenzong praised and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong came to the throne, Hao was again appointed grand academician of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies. He memorialized urging the Emperor to promote literary governance, enlarge the Imperial University, and exempt scholars from corvée labor, and Wenzong approved every proposal.

sentences.zh: 顥先後居集賢，署薦士牘累數百，有訐之者，顥曰：「吾寧以謬舉受罰，蔽賢誠所不忍。

translations.literal: Hao successively served in the Academy of Scholarly Worthies and signed recommendation documents for scholars numbering in the hundreds. When someone denounced him, Hao said: "I would rather be punished for mistaken recommendation than bear to conceal the worthy."
translations.idiomatic: During his years in the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, Hao signed hundreds of recommendations for scholars. When someone accused him of favoritism, he said, "I would rather be punished for a mistaken recommendation than conceal a worthy man."

sentences.zh: 」順帝元統初，顥扈蹕行幸上都，至龍虎台，帝命造膝前，而握其手曰：「卿累朝老臣，更事多矣，凡議政事，宜極言無隱。

translations.literal: " At the beginning of Yuantong under Shundi, Hao accompanied the imperial procession on the journey to Shangdu; when they reached Longhu Terrace, the Emperor ordered him brought before his knee and grasped his hand, saying: "You are an old minister of successive reigns and have seen many affairs; in all deliberations on government you should speak to the utmost without concealment."
translations.idiomatic: " Early in Shundi's Yuantong reign, Hao accompanied the court to Shangdu. At Longhu Terrace the Emperor summoned him forward, took his hand, and said, "You are a veteran of many reigns who has seen much. In all affairs of state, speak plainly and hold nothing back."

sentences.zh: 」顥頓首謝不敏。

translations.literal: " Hao bowed his head and thanked him, declaring himself unworthy.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao bowed and thanked him, declaring himself unworthy of such trust.

sentences.zh: 顥每集議，其言無不剴切，後至元四年，致政，命食全俸於家。

translations.literal: Whenever Hao joined in collective deliberation, his words were invariably incisive and earnest. In the fourth year of Later Zhiyuan he retired from office and was ordered to receive his full salary at home.
translations.idiomatic: In every council Hao's words were incisive and earnest. In the fourth year of Later Zhiyuan he retired, and was granted his full salary at home.

sentences.zh: 明年卒，年七十六。

translations.literal: The next year he died, aged seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year at the age of seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 至正十四年，贈攄誠秉義佐理功臣、光祿大夫、河南江北等處行中書省平章政事、柱國，追封薊國公，諡文忠。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhizheng he was posthumously granted the title Meritorious Subject Who Expands Sincerity, Upholds Righteousness, and Assists Governance, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Grand Councillor of the Henan and Jiangbei Branch Secretariat, and Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Duke of Ji, with the posthumous name Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In 1354 he was posthumously honored as a meritorious subject who expanded sincerity, upheld righteousness, and assisted governance, with the titles of Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Grand Councillor of the Henan and Jiangbei Branch Secretariat, and Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Duke of Ji, and given the posthumous name Wenzhong, "Cultured and Loyal."

sentences.zh: 顥出入禁闥數十年，樂談人善，而惡聞人過。

translations.literal: Hao entered and left the forbidden gates for several decades; he delighted in speaking of others' virtues and hated to hear of others' faults.
translations.idiomatic: For decades Hao moved in and out of the inner palace. He delighted in praising others' virtues and refused to hear their faults spoken.

sentences.zh: 大夫士因其薦拔以至顯列，有終身莫知所自者，是以結知人主，上下無有怨尤。

translations.literal: Great ministers and scholars reached eminent rank through his recommendation and advancement until they attained high office; some never knew in their whole lives from whom it came. Thus he won the sovereign's trust, and above and below there was no resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Many officials rose to high rank through his recommendations until they attained eminent office; some never knew in their whole lives who had helped them. He won the sovereign's deep trust, and neither court nor people bore him resentment.

sentences.zh: 歐陽玄為國子祭酒，與顥同考試國子伴讀，每出一卷，顥必拾而觀之，苟得其片言善，即以置選列，為之色喜。

translations.literal: Ouyang Xuan was Chancellor of the Imperial University; together with Hao he examined the university student-companions. Whenever a paper was produced, Hao would pick it up and read it; if he found even a single good phrase, he would place the writer in the selected list and show pleasure on his face.
translations.idiomatic: When Ouyang Xuan was chancellor of the Imperial University, he and Hao jointly examined student-companions. Hao would read every paper submitted; if he found even one good phrase, he would place the writer on the selected list and beam with pleasure.

sentences.zh: 玄歎曰：「陳公之心，蓋篤於仁而逾於厚者，真可使鄙夫寬、薄夫敦矣。」

translations.literal: Xuan sighed and said: "Master Chen's heart is surely devoted to benevolence and surpasses even generosity; he can truly make the mean-spirited broad and the shallow-hearted sincere."
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xuan sighed and said, "Master Chen's heart is rooted in benevolence beyond ordinary generosity. He could truly make the mean-spirited broad-minded and the shallow-hearted sincere."

sentences.zh: 次子敬伯，至正中仕為中書參知政事，歷左丞、右丞，二十七年，拜中書平章政事。

translations.literal: His second son Jingbo, during Zhizheng served as Assistant Administrator of the Central Secretariat, passed through Left Chancellor and Right Chancellor, and in the twenty-seventh year was appointed Grand Councillor of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Jingbo served during the Zhizheng reign as assistant administrator of the Central Secretariat, rose through the left and right chancellorships, and in the twenty-seventh year was appointed grand councillor.
